recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-34405 unless a separate editorial pass wants to improve nearby prose, which is outside this issue because the requested regex behavior is already present.
issue_request: FHIR-34405 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request asking that the references page regex for a reference consistent with a FHIR API allow an optional #fragment suffix for contained-resource references. The approved resolution was to append an optional group matching #[A-Za-z0-9\-.]{1,64}.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git commit 9af4169b9d53037cd7d966019b5ed326d6dc1ac2, which added an optional (#[A-Za-z0-9\-.]{1,64})? suffix to source/references.html. Later commit f9a77c9edb5bca4f6a60d0d6c55b402a2500a9ee changed the generated id macro token from [%id_regex%] to [%regex id%] while preserving the fragment suffix.
additional_context: source/references.html is the FHIR core references page source corresponding to Jira's FHIR-core-references related page. FHIR-34345, a separate contained-resource history clarification, supports the current regex order by approving [type]/[id]/_history/[version]#[containedId] as a valid shape. FHIR-I minutes from 2022-03-21 record the 11-0-0 Persuasive motion for FHIR-34405, and Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the combined branch already has the requested optional suffix in source/references.html. The unescaped # in the displayed regex is equivalent to Jira's escaped literal \# in this regex context.

related_jiras.note: Clarified that references may target contained resources within a versioned containing resource, aligning with the regex order [type]/[id]/_history/[version]#[containedId].
